question: What is South Africa's current legal and operating perimeter for crypto-asset services, stablecoins and tokenised money; how do licensing, financial-intelligence, exchange-control and tax rules interact; and where do final money, correction and customer loss remain?
bluf: South Africa has an operating but layered crypto-service regime: the FSCA licenses covered FAIS advice, intermediary and investment-management services; FIC Item 22 and Directive 9 impose separate AML and travel-rule duties; SARS applies tax and CARF reporting; and SARB and FinSurv retain currency, exchange-control and settlement authority. Crypto is not legal tender or SARB-backed, and a dedicated prudential stablecoin-issuer regime still was not located. The private market is nevertheless operating. BlockTower, not Standard Bank, is the issuer of the live rand stablecoin ZARU; Standard Bank holds bank-deposit reserves and provides securities custody while Sanlam manages the money-market portion. A 31 July agreed-upon-procedures snapshot reported 52.946 million ZARU in circulation, R53.717 million of eligible reserves and 101.46% coverage, but no audit opinion or assurance conclusion. Standard Bank separately reports more than R1 trillion through its Aroko blockchain-enabled conventional cross-border processing rail. Absa markets a current institutional digital-asset custody service using Ripple technology. Nedbank's planned ZAR/USDC conversion, liquidity and daily-net-settlement arrangement remains a conditional phased rollout with no reviewed production receipt. The six current systemically important banks are Absa, Standard Bank, FirstRand, Nedbank, Investec and Capitec; their states range from live custody or reserve-banking to pilots, preparation and bounded negative results. SAMOS remains final central-bank money. Khokha 2 was a proof of concept, retail CBDC is not being implemented immediately, and the August cross-border Crypto Assets Manual remained a proposal after its 30 September comment deadline.

authority.summary: Parliament, the Minister of Finance and National Treasury own law and policy; FSCA licenses and supervises covered FAIS crypto services; SARB, the Prudential Authority and FinSurv own banking, currency, exchange control and settlement; FIC owns AML/CFT/FP; SARS owns tax and CARF; courts and tribunals own adjudication.
authority.boundary: Financial-services authorization, AML registration, bank prudential status, exchange-control permission, tax reporting, settlement operation and adjudication are different capacities.

legal_objects.summary: The record separates the FAIS-defined crypto financial product, FIC Item 22 CASP activities, private stablecoin claims, custody and provider books, rand bank balances, legal tender, SAMOS central-bank money, tax-reportable crypto assets and experimental Khokha 2 wCBDC, bank token and tokenised debenture records.
legal_objects.boundary: A common digital interface does not merge issuer liability, direct redemption, customer title, custody, tax characterization, legal tender or final central-bank money.

permitted_activities.summary: Covered advice, intermediary and investment-management services require FAIS authorization. FIC Item 22 separately covers client-facing fiat/crypto and crypto/crypto exchange, transfer, safekeeping/control and specified issuer-offer services. Ownership or use is not made legal tender, and cross-border activity remains subject to exchange-control permission.
permitted_activities.boundary: Lawful possession, financial-service authorization, CASP AML status, bank access, exchange-control permission and successful operation are separate propositions.

entry_gates.summary: A covered provider must join the exact legal person and service to an FSCA FSP authorization or representative status, fit-and-proper and conduct duties, FIC Item 22 registration and AML controls. Banking/payment access and any FinSurv permission or individual allowance remain additional gates.
entry_gates.boundary: Application, approval, exact activity, current compliance, bank account, authorized-dealer processing, technical availability and transaction execution are separate clocks.

named_operating_actors.summary: SARB reported 310 FSCA-licensed CASPs at 31 March 2026. Its Tether scale figure names Luno, VALR and AltCoinTrader only as the three measured platforms. SARB currently designates Absa, Standard Bank, FirstRand, Nedbank, Investec and Capitec as systemically important banks. In that bank layer, Standard Bank provides ZARU reserve banking and securities custody and operates Aroko; Absa markets institutional digital-asset custody; Nedbank has announced a conditional Crypto.com ZAR/USDC rollout; Absa, FirstRand, Nedbank and Standard Bank were active Khokha 2 participants; Investec participated in the broader project work and describes sandboxed capability; Capitec supplies risk warnings but no reviewed digital-asset product. FSCA publishes regulated-entity search surfaces, but this pass did not establish a cutoff export joining every legal person, service category, condition, suspension and active domain.
named_operating_actors.boundary: SIFI designation, a dated CASP licence count, brand, group, bank legal person, FSP, stablecoin issuer, reserve account, custodian, technology vendor, proof of concept and production service are different roles.

claims_and_backing.summary: Crypto is not SARB-issued, backed or guaranteed, and no dedicated prudential stablecoin-issuer licence was located. ZARU is a current private issuer structure: Loop South Africa, trading as BlockTower, is the issuer and FSP; Standard Bank holds cash and deposit reserves and provides securities custody; Sanlam Investment Management holds or manages the money-market portion; and Moore performs monthly agreed-upon procedures. The 31 July snapshot reported R23.314 million of cash and bank deposits plus R30.403 million of money-market funds against 52.946 million ZARU. Direct mint and redemption are limited by the whitepaper to verified institutional clients; retail or other holders use authorized partners. The report says Loop is the bank account holder and fund investor, so a token holder has an issuer redemption claim rather than a bank deposit in their own name. Khokha 2 wCBDC and bank tokens were experimental liabilities inside a proof of concept.
claims_and_backing.boundary: FSP authorization, asset custody, issuer debt, reserve account title, reserve-asset custody, direct redemption, agreed-upon procedures, deposit insurance and sovereign guarantee are distinct claims; the AUP report is not an audit or assurance opinion.

domestic_rails.summary: SAMOS is SARB's production RTGS and supplies final and irrevocable settlement when funds or eligible collateral support the instruction. PayShap is a production fast-retail payment layer. CASP books and blockchain transactions are separate records, while SADC-RTGS is a conventional regional fiat rail.
domestic_rails.boundary: Retail speed, bank credit, central-bank finality, CASP execution, chain confirmation, custody and customer title are different records.

cross_border_routes.summary: Directive 9 carries travel-rule information for covered domestic and cross-border transfers; existing FinSurv rules govern allowances and exchange control; and the August 2026 Crypto Assets Manual proposes a future authorized-CASP framework. Its 30 September comment deadline passed without a reviewed final instrument by the cutoff. Standard Bank's Aroko is genuine recurring blockchain-enabled cross-border bank processing with more than R1 trillion since inception, but its public description is an automated conventional FX-payment and standing-settlement-instruction rail, not a stablecoin or crypto transfer. Nedbank's ZAR/USDC route is announced and conditional, not yet supported by a production receipt. None proves a crypto country-pair route through payer, beneficiary, funding, FX, token transfer, final receipt, failure and correction.
cross_border_routes.boundary: Reporting duty, policy proposal, provider capability, aggregate activity or a regional fiat rail is not an observed country-pair route; the map carries zero arcs.

operating_state.summary: FSCA licensing, FIC Item 22 controls, Directive 9, ordinary tax treatment, CARF reporting, SAMOS and PayShap are operating. Existing exchange-control guidance remains current. ZARU is live for qualifying institutional distribution with a current on-chain supply and reserve report; Absa's institutional custody is a current marketed service; Standard Bank's Aroko is recurring conventional cross-border production. Nedbank's ZAR/USDC arrangement remains a planned, phased and permission-conditioned rollout. Khokha 2 is concluded experimentation, the retail-CBDC position rejects immediate implementation, and the 2026 capital-flow and crypto manuals remain proposals.
operating_state.boundary: Effective rule, licensed financial service, issuer launch, reserve-bank service, custody product, announced rollout, conventional blockchain processing, completed proof of concept, policy position, consultation draft, first transaction and recurring production are separate states.

scale.summary: SARB reported 310 FSCA-licensed CASPs at 31 March 2026 and almost R27 billion of Tether on-chain transactions across Luno, VALR and AltCoinTrader for the year to 30 April 2026, with Silver Sixpence as the data source. ZARU's 31 July AUP snapshot reported 52,946,200.12 tokens in circulation and R53,716,955.21 of eligible reserves, a 101.46% ratio. Standard Bank reports Aroko processed more than R1 trillion since inception; its 2023 report had identified 21,682 conventional cross-border transactions worth R114 billion that year. The 2024 payment report separately disclosed PayShap use. No public complete national CASP or stablecoin settlement aggregate was established.
scale.boundary: Licence count is not active firms; three-platform private-source volume is not a national total; a one-time issuer AUP snapshot is not continuous solvency or redemption performance; Aroko bank-processing volume is not crypto or stablecoin volume.

stress.summary: SARB judged crypto and stablecoin activity not currently systemic while monitoring growth, cross-border links and regulatory gaps. FSCA/FIC authorization, inspection, risk management, records and travel-rule controls are prospective safeguards. ZARU's AUP report reconciled the July snapshot above par but disclaimed any audit opinion, assurance conclusion or internal-control testing; management remained responsible for supply, circulation and reserve definitions. Absa describes hardware-protected authorization, deterministic key derivation and recoverability, but no public customer count, assets under custody, outage or recovery test was located. The reviewed bundle does not supply a national provider-failure, stablecoin-run, custody-shortfall or consumer-loss series.
stress.boundary: A systemic-risk judgment, inspection, control or warning is not evidence of firm solvency, stress survival, quantified customer loss or recovery.

correction_and_loss.summary: Correction can involve CASP books, blockchain control, bank procedures, FinSurv regularization, FSCA/FIC action and court or tribunal disposition. FinSurv's 10%-40% settlement mechanism concerns exchange-control contraventions; SAMOS finality governs the accepted fiat entry. Neither mechanism makes a failed crypto claimant whole.
correction_and_loss.boundary: Technical reversal, record correction, license action, regulatory settlement, asset freeze, seizure, insolvency recognition and customer restitution are separate clocks.

evidence_boundary.summary: The baseline uses an effective gazette, current regulator and central-bank publications, official payment and stability reports, bank-authored product materials, and the issuer's legal and reserve documents. The private source behind SARB's Tether figure is labeled. ZARU's Moore report is an agreed-upon-procedures engagement, not an audit or assurance conclusion, and its issuer-defined classifications are kept visible. Bank statements prove the bank's stated product or role, not regulatory endorsement, complete legal title or independent operating receipts. Stale all-regime wording on one SARB FAQ is used only for its currency/FX boundary. Existing owners remain context rather than silently updated sources.
evidence_boundary.boundary: Fresh country research is not Chronicle promotion, investment advice, publication authority or permission to hand-edit generated projections.
